newsitem.title: USA: NYC might delay debt sale until late Sept - source.
newsitem.headline: NYC might delay debt sale until late Sept - source.

text.p: New York City might delay by a couple of weeks a planned note offering that could total as much as $1.5 billion to late September or early October, a city source suggested on Tuesday.

The source, who spoke on condition of anonymity and stressed that the offering's timing and size still are tentative, explained the deal likely would include about $1.5 billion of revenue anticipation notes (RANs). This debt would mature in April and June.
Further, he speculated New York City is considering sellling from $750 million to $1 billion of general obligation bonds at the same time.

The timing and size of the sales could not be immediately confirmed, as a city official said he did not expect to finalize the details of the offering for another few days. But in late August, the city said it was planning to sell about $750 million of new and refunding bonds in November through its underwriting syndicate.
Another $75 million of taxable bonds were expected to be sold through competitive auction in November.

The city officials also had said they planned to issue about $1.6 billion of RANS in mid- to late-September, explaining the issues would mature in March and late June. The offering was expected to be sold competitively.
